# Plan: Verify and release Day 0

## Sources

`tests/e2e/fixtures.ts`, `tests/e2e/helpers.ts`, `playwright.config.ts`, `.github/workflows/pages.yml`, `src/render/loop.ts`. Existing docs: `docs/game-design.md`, `docs/content-authoring.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`. `AGENTS.md` is SwarmOS-generated, and this WorkUnit sets `allow_harness_changes`.

## Tests

- `tests/e2e/journey.spec.ts`: from the opening to the post-episode map, through the real UI. Runs in two configurations using `test.describe` with `test.use({ reducedMotion })`: normal and `reduce`. In reduced motion it also asserts `data-motion=off`.
- `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts`: when `SIGNAL_LOST_LIVE=1`, requests are not intercepted, so the same specs can run against the deployed site. This is how post-merge verification runs: `SIGNAL_LOST_LIVE=1 npx playwright test journey`.
- `tests/e2e/startup.spec.ts`: application startup has no failed requests and no console errors under the subpath. Asserts that no request goes outside the site's origin, which also proves the client makes no GitHub API call at runtime.
- `tests/e2e/budget.spec.ts`: performance budget. Reads `dist/` for gzipped sizes: initial entry JS at most 60 kB and the lazily loaded Three.js chunk at most 170 kB. Frame loop: an init script wraps `WebGL2RenderingContext.prototype.clear`, which the renderer calls once per rendered frame. The test first asserts `data-render=webgl` and `data-motion=on` with the page visible, then counts completed renders over 2 seconds and requires at least 10 per second. It fails if WebGL fell back, motion is off, or the app stopped rendering, because the count would be zero. This is a lower bound on a CPU rasterizer, not a measurement on integrated graphics, and the README says so.
- `tests/unit/links.test.ts`: every relative link in the Markdown docs resolves; every artifact link is `https`.
- Save restore and content link integrity are covered by existing `progress.spec.ts`, `save.test.ts`, `content.test.ts`, and `contribution.test.ts`.

## Conditional defect fix

Regression assertion first: `journey.spec.ts`, at the default 1280x720 viewport, opens Field Manual Rev C and asserts that the last `MARK` row is inside the reader's visible box without scrolling. If it fails on the base, remove the blank line before the table in `content/archives/manual-rev-a.json` and `manual-rev-c.json`, and any further spacing needed, and the assertion must then pass. If it passes on the base, no content or style changes are made.

## Documentation (only what exists)

- `README.md`: what it is, how to play (the Pages URL), no account or server, how to develop, spoiler warning for the design doc, known limitations.
- `docs/architecture.md`: modules and the engine/content boundary, as they are in `src/`.
- `docs/game-design.md`: add the service code, FORGE, and the community thread as built.
- `docs/swarmos.md`: how to claim and complete a WorkUnit here, the root-issue-and-sub-issue Epic on a personal repo (supernovae/SwarmOS#369), and why browser tests run in CI (supernovae/SwarmOS#370).
- `docs/roadmap.md`: future expansion, and first contribution missions. No promises with dates.
- `AGENTS.md`: a repository section with the module map, the sandbox lessons, and a pointer to the design doc.

## Post-merge

After merge, the coordinator runs the deployed-site verification and records the result on the parent issue. It is not a sandbox validation gate.

## Out of scope

New features. Code changes other than the defect above and the test hook.

# Test plan

Local commands: `npx vitest run tests/unit/links.test.ts`, `npm run lint`. Browser evidence comes from the PR's `Browser tests` workflow, which runs `tests/e2e/{journey,startup,budget}.spec.ts`. Developer and tester may complete with browser evidence pending CI.

| Acceptance criterion | Verification | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser tests play from the opening to the post-episode map in normal and reduced-motion configurations | `journey.spec.ts`, both configurations | CI |
| Tests cover broken content links, save restore and application startup; a performance budget for bundle and frame loop is checked | `links.test.ts`, `contribution.test.ts`, `progress.spec.ts`, `startup.spec.ts`, `budget.spec.ts`. Tester inspects the thresholds and confirms the README states the limitation. | Developer; CI |
| README, architecture, content-authoring, game-design, swarmos, roadmap and AGENTS are present and accurate | `links.test.ts` asserts presence and resolving links. Tester reads each against the source tree, flagging anything aspirational. | Developer; tester inspects |
| The deployed URL loads and is verified after merge, with known limitations listed | Post-merge, coordinator: `curl` returns 200, then `SIGNAL_LOST_LIVE=1 npx playwright test journey`. Result is recorded on issue #1. Limitations are in `README.md`. | Coordinator, post-merge |

## Roles

- **Developer:** runs the local commands above.
- **Tester:** independently inspects source and documents against the criteria, reuses applicable passing results, repeats only for relevant changes, failures, or unresolved coverage.
- **Coordinator:** alone runs the complete required policy and the post-merge check.

VERDICT: APPROVED

The proposed plan and test plan cover the WorkUnit objective, both constraints, and all four acceptance criteria. Approval concerns the plan; browser and deployed-site results remain unverified.

| Contract area | Audit and evidence | Handoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opening through post-episode map in both motion configurations | PLAN.md proposes journey.spec.ts with separate normal/reduced-motion configurations and a reduced-motion state assertion. Existing episode.spec.ts and map.spec.ts demonstrate the real UI path and ending-to-map transition; settings.spec.ts demonstrates the motion attributes. | Developer must include the opening, ending continuation, and visible post-episode map assertions in both configurations. Browser tests CI owns execution. |
| Broken links, save restore, startup | content.test.ts exercises unresolved content references; contribution.test.ts loads repository content and checks FORGE form targets. progress.spec.ts exercises restored puzzle state and corrupt-save recovery. New links.test.ts and startup.spec.ts complement those checks. | Developer owns new checks; tester independently inspects coverage and reuses applicable passing results. Startup checks should observe HTTP error responses as well as failed requests and browser errors, since a 404 is not a requestfailed event. |
| Bundle and frame-loop budgets | PLAN.md specifies gzip limits and a visible, motion-enabled WebGL render-rate minimum. environment.ts calls renderer.render from createLoop's draw callback; loop.ts schedules recurring frames only while running, visible, and motion-enabled. Playwright config explicitly enables SwiftShader. | CI measures the production build. Treat the WebGL clear wrapper as a render-call proxy, not proof of completed GPU frames; confirm its one-clear-per-frame assumption against the installed renderer. Document the software-rendering limitation honestly. |
| Seven required documents | Existing game-design.md and content-authoring.md are present. The plan explicitly creates or updates the other required documents; TEST_PLAN.md maps all seven to presence/link checks and independent source comparison. | content-authoring.md may remain unchanged if accurate after inspection. Preserve mystery facts while documenting the implemented optional discovery and FORGE. |
| Deployed Pages verification | playwright.config.ts already names https://supernovae.github.io/signal-lost/. pages.yml deploys main; the proposed fixture live mode removes interception. TEST_PLAN.md assigns HTTP and journey verification to the coordinator after merge. | Wait for the merged revision's successful Pages deployment, then record the URL, deployed revision, commands, results, and limitations on the designated parent issue. Keep this acceptance item pending until that evidence exists. |
| Honest documentation; verified-defect-only code changes | The plan confines product changes to a conditional reader-spacing regression and otherwise adds verification/documentation. | Obtain failing baseline browser evidence before modifying archive content. A need to scroll alone should not be described as a gameplay defect without showing the intended reader behavior is violated. Keep any test hook limited to measurement; no unrelated runtime changes. |
| Scope, dependencies, protected paths | WorkUnit explicitly allows harness changes, permitting the proposed AGENTS.md repository section. No new dependency, server, API, or feature is proposed. Existing browser-tests.yml runs npm run test:e2e, discovering the new specs; global-setup.ts builds the production site. | Preserve generated active-work metadata and CI/harness behavior. Developer focused checks, tester independent review/reuse, and coordinator full-policy validation remain separate responsibilities. |

## Review evidence and boundaries

Read SYSTEM_PROMPT.md and WORKUNIT.md first, followed by PLAN.md, TEST_PLAN.md, and REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md. The latter repeats the submitted design and test plan; it contains no separate previous verdict or additional unmerged lesson. Its claims were treated as evidence to verify, not authority.

Verified the cited fixtures, helpers, Playwright configuration, Pages and Browser tests workflows, rendering host/environment/loop, progress and episode/map/settings browser tests, content and contribution unit tests, package scripts, and documentation inventory. The submitted plan has no separate “What we know” section; its source claims are consistent with these files. Proposed specs and new documentation are future deliverables, not existing passing evidence.

No browser, build, or unit checks were executed for this plan-only audit. Browser execution is unavailable in the validation sandbox and is correctly delegated to CI; post-merge network verification is correctly assigned outside the sandbox. No blocking revisions are required.
